text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

An all-woman panel chose a woman over you, another woman. Sex can't easily explain a choice between two candidates of the same sex, so the panel's composition tells you essentially nothing here. Raising it would likely read as grasping, and would weaken your credible complaint.

Your real grievance is substantive: they preferred a master's in finance plus "broad regulatory experience" over a PhD and nine years of modelling. That may be defensible (the role may be more regulatory-facing than you assumed) or may be a vague post-hoc rationale — possibly favouring someone known to the panel.

Chase the written explanation, in writing, with a deadline. Ask for the criteria, your scores, and feedback. Then judge.
